payload.text:
Arma un sitio web minimalista sobre mi grupo y sus capacidades. Lo usaré como carta de presentación ante colegas cuando no pueda estar presente

​1. HERO
​Título:
GENÓMICA Y BIODIVERSIDAD
​Subtítulo:
Biología evolutiva, entomología y ciencia de datos en el Neotrópico.
​CTA:
[ Conocer Investigación ]
​2. IDENTIDAD
​"Somos un laboratorio interdisciplinar en la Universidad del Norte. Integramos la biología molecular y la entomología con el análisis de datos masivos.
​Fomentamos una visión integral donde estudiantes de biología y geología convergen para responder preguntas evolutivas usando herramientas genómicas."
​3. LÍNEAS DE INVESTIGACIÓN
​01. Historia Evolutiva y Biogeografía
​Investigamos cómo el paisaje y los cambios ambientales históricos han moldeado la genética de las poblaciones actuales.
​Enfoque: Filogeografía, Genética de Poblaciones, Interfaz Geo-Biológica.
​02. Entomología Molecular y Urbana
​Estudiamos la diversidad de insectos y sus adaptaciones genéticas a entornos naturales y urbanos.
​Enfoque: Vectores, Biodiversidad en el Antropoceno, Taxonomía Integrativa.
​03. Ciencia de Datos (Data Agnostic)
​Desarrollamos estrategias bioinformáticas flexibles, adaptables a cualquier tipo de dato biológico, desde secuencias virales hasta comunidades complejas.
​Enfoque: Genómica Comparativa, Análisis de De Novo, Modelado.
​4. CAPACIDADES
​Campo y Colecciones
​Monitoreo de biodiversidad en gradientes ambientales.
​Identificación taxonómica y morfológica de insectos.
​Colección de tejidos y ADNs.
​Laboratorio (Genómica)
​Monitoreo molecular mediante ADN Ambiental (eDNA).
​Extracción de ADN/ARN de alta complejidad.
​Preparación de librerías para secuenciación (NGS).
​Bioinformática
​Ensamblaje y anotación de genomas/transcriptomas.
​Desarrollo de pipelines de análisis a medida.
​Datación molecular y filogenómica.
​5. INVESTIGADOR PRINCIPAL
​Rafik Neme, Ph.D.
Biología Evolutiva & Genómica Computacional
​"Mi trabajo conecta la teoría evolutiva molecular con la conservación del Caribe. Uso el genoma como un archivo histórico para entender el origen de la novedad biológica."
​Hitos:
​Evolución Molecular: Descubrimiento de genes de novo a partir de ADN no codificante.
​Dinámica Genómica: Estudios sobre plasticidad extrema del genoma y transcripción.
​Aplicación Local: Uso de eDNA y genómica para catalogar la biodiversidad colombiana.
​6. EL EQUIPO
​Un grupo colaborativo formado por:
​Biólogos y Entomólogos.
​Estudiantes de Geología con formación en herramientas moleculares.
​Analistas de Datos y Bioinformáticos.

**Analyzing the Goal**

I've been dissecting the request, focusing on the core objective: a simple, effective portfolio site for this research group. My thinking is centered on who the audience is - academic peers. This directly influences the necessary content and tone.


**Structuring the App**

I'm structuring the application now. It's evolving into an `index.html` with a Tailwind CDN, a React root in `index.tsx`, and an `App.tsx` handling sections. I'm building out components for Hero, Identity, Research Lines, Capabilities, PI info, and Team. I'm exploring how to incorporate `d3` or `recharts` for a small data visualization. Minimalist design is my priority. The plan is to create React components, using Typescript, with Tailwind for styling, and Lucide for icons.


**Developing the Structure**

My current focus is fleshing out the application architecture. I'm building React components for each section: Hero, Identity, Research Lines, Capabilities, PI, and Team. I'm considering a Recharts component for a subtle data visualization. I've designed the footer and added a sticky navigation. The goal is a minimalist single-page design with Tailwind.


**Defining the Components**

I'm now iterating on the component definitions. My focus is on the basic boilerplate, like imports and types. I've blocked out the `Hero`, which is full-screen, centered text with a dark gradient overlay on the background image. The `Identity` component will be a simple text block emphasizing the interdisciplinary nature. The `Research Lines` are a 3-column grid with Lucide icons (Globe/Map for History, Bug for Entomology, and Database/Binary for Data).

I'm structuring the `Capabilities` section as a clean, responsive card-based layout, organized into Field, Lab, and Bioinfo categories. I'm also planning a small `Recharts` bar chart visualizing the "Interdisciplinary Mix" data (Biology, Geology, Data) to meet the requirement for a chart.


**Integrating Visuals**

I've decided on a Radar Chart for the "Research Lines" section, visualizing the distribution across different research focuses. I'm now crafting the `PI` profile card with the photo on the left and text on the right, and the `Team` component will use a simple list or grid format. I've initiated the step-by-step coding with the `metadata.json`, `index.html`, and `index.tsx` files. I'm integrating Tailwind in `index.html`. In `App.tsx`, I'm combining components.  I've created the `Navigation.tsx`, `Hero.tsx`, and `ResearchLines.tsx` components.  I'm building out the `Capabilities.tsx` with check icons for each item.


**Finalizing the Details**

I'm now polishing the final elements. I'm focusing on incorporating the PI's quote and milestones within the `PrincipalInvestigator` component and defining necessary data structures in `types.ts`, if needed. I'm also ensuring all the text is accurately translated into Spanish and that "Universidad del Norte" is present. To add some subtle animation, I plan to use Tailwind classes for fade-ins and explore simple transitions for a smooth, minimalist aesthetic. `lucide-react` icons are planned. Finally, I'm confirming that the design adheres to the constraints, including the single XML block, absence of external CSS, and React 18 version.


**Coding the Radar Chart**

I'm now implementing the Radar Chart for the Research Lines, visualizing the lab's focus on Evolution, Genomics, Ecology, Data Science, and Conservation. I've switched to consistent science-themed images using picsum.photos for the visual aesthetic. I'm focusing on ensuring responsiveness, particularly with the navigation, to handle the mobile-first layout. I also refined the PI component for the final visual polish.


**Formulating the Output**

I'm now drafting the XML structure for the single-page application. I'm prioritizing semantic HTML and accessibility, ensuring proper nesting and use of ARIA attributes where necessary. The goal is to represent the entire content within a single XML block for deployment. I've translated all required text to spanish. I am working on the final touch-ups, like ensuring correct link and text translations for the PI section.

**Evaluating Website Needs**

I've begun dissecting the prompt, specifically the need to refine the website for "Genómica y Biodiversidad." I'm pinpointing the core objectives and cataloging all the raw content provided, like research lines and ongoing projects. This information is crucial for pinpointing the most crucial site elements. My current focus is on prioritizing content for clarity and impact, readying for structural implementation.


**Prioritizing Content Clarity**

Now, I'm focusing on the "Identity" section, integrating the information from the input text to bolster its core message. I'm carefully considering how to represent key concepts like "Hormigas del Bosque Seco" and "Elasticidad Genómica" within the minimalist style constraint. Also, I'm streamlining the "Principal Investigator" section per specifications and adding the "Other Projects" list. The overall structure is solidified as: `Hero`, `Identity`, `ResearchLines`, `Capabilities`, `PrincipalInvestigator`, `Team`, `Footer`.


**Revising Research Focus**

The "ResearchLines" section demands a significant update. I'm restructuring the section to mirror the four key areas: Molecular Evolution, Insect Diversity, Caribbean Ecosystems, and Outreach. Previously generic placeholders are now replaced with detailed descriptions and project names. I'm leaning toward a grid layout of categorized cards for a clean, user-friendly presentation. The "Desde la evolución..." blurb will be included here.


**Integrating Project Details**

I'm now integrating the detailed "Other Projects" list (Dipteros, moscas, eDNA, morfometria) into the `ResearchLines` component, ensuring a unified structure. These projects naturally fit within existing research categories. I'm focusing on weaving these details into the narrative smoothly. Additionally, I'm removing the image from the `PrincipalInvestigator` section, adhering to the feedback, and incorporating the mentioned affiliations to establish credibility.


**Refining Website Elements**

I'm now revising the footer, updating contact details to include Office 630J, a phone extension, and a specific email, along with links to Max Planck and Pew. Navigation updates are also in progress, linking to "Grupo," "Investigación," "Capacidades," and "Contacto." Minor adjustments include the Hero subtitle, the Identity section's "Desde la evolución..." text, and the Principal Investigator section without the image. I'll center the text and highlight key areas.


**Organizing Project Data**

I'm currently crafting the data structure for the `ResearchLines` component, specifically focusing on the new grid layout with project listings for each of the four categories. I've compiled the detailed project names and descriptions for "Evolución Molecular y Genómica" and "Diversidad de Insectos" into respective categories. Next, I'll be incorporating the "Other" projects like Dipteros, Moscas, and Morfometria within the Insect Diversity section, organizing them into a unified list. This effort will bring forth the visual organization using clean typography and perhaps small icons. My main focus is to ensure the layout is responsive, looking good on different screen sizes.


**Implementing Component Refinement**

Now, I'm working through the code changes. I'm focusing on the PrincipalInvestigator component, aiming for a classy, image-less design using a large serif font and a flat card style. The Footer is also being updated for better address and link handling. I'm actively verifying the minimalist style: ample whitespace, a limited palette (Slate/Emerald), and crisp typography (Inter/Playfair). Simultaneously, I'm organizing the XML files: the navigation, hero, identity, and a complete rewrite for research lines.


**Refining Code Implementation**

I'm now implementing the code, focusing on `components/PrincipalInvestigator.tsx` and `components/Footer.tsx`. The PI component is now image-free with the requested large serif font and flat card style; the footer has updated contact details and links, and I've included a "Publicaciones" link in the nav for completeness, despite the missing content. I'm verifying the minimalist design principles as I go. ResearchLines has a clear grid layout. The "Other Projects" are now integrated into appropriate ResearchLines categories.


**Constructing XML Structure**

I'm now generating the XML, meticulously integrating all research projects into the grid layout within `ResearchLines`. "Morfometria geometrica de hormigas..." will be under Insectos. I've removed the Radar chart for a text-centric approach. I'll summarize the PI blurb, highlighting key achievements. Finally, I'm adding "Enlaces de Interés" to the Footer.
